notes.title: Update notes (4th June 2025)
notes.content:
[b]Full changelog:[/b]
[list]
[*] Chapter 0: Fixed hotel doors sometimes opening to wrong directions
[*] Added "deletePlayerPref" command to the developer console - Example: "deletePlayerPref vr-tracking-origin-mode" command restores the VR tracking mode back to seated mode
[*] (VR) Improved standing / roomscale VR tracking mode - reduces the chances of camera getting stuck on the floor when enabling the setting
[*] (VR) Fixed bugs related to water slide entering: players could get stuck inside the environment, players wouldn't be teleported to the exit position when the "skip water slides" setting was enabled
[*] (VR) Added a tiny bit of smoothing to free movement to help eliminate judder
[*] (VR) Optimized some volumetric effects in Chapter 0
[*] (VR) Added "haptics intensity" slider to gameplay setting
[*] (VR) Disabled transparent material screen space reflections because of compatibility issue with water surface shader
[/list]

We are investigating and pursuing performance optimizations with the goal of switching the rendering mode to multi-pass rendering in the future. Screen space water reflections do not have the misalignment issue when using multi-pass rendering, but it does come with a larger performance overhead when compared to the currently active single-pass instanced mode.

Thank you very much for the VR related feedback and every bit of support we've received thus far! We'll continue fixing bugs and working towards those performance improvements.

Also - VR support will be added to the Demo version hopefully tomorrow. We'll post an update about it once it is available.

notes.title: Chapter 0 is Here – A Free New Level
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

The waters of POOLS just got deeper. Chapter 0 - a brand-new free level, is now available!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/UI67XaJ.jpeg[/img]

This free content update is our way of saying “thank you” to all of you here. Over the past year, POOLS has grown beyond our wildest dreams, with over 4,000 Overwhelmingly Positive Steam reviews. Thanks to you, our small team has been able to work on POOLS as a real job. We are a fully-fledged, real studio. So thank you for making our dreams come true. But that’s not all. A free [b]PC VR update is coming May 30, 2025[/b], letting you experience POOLS in an entirely new way. Plus, App Store and PS5 releases, along with PS VR2 support, are also planned for later this year.

Tensori

notes.title: VR Beta update - all chapters now available for owners of the game
notes.content:
We're pleased to report that owners of the game now have access to every chapter in VR Beta! 

The full release of PC VR mode is scheduled for early 2025. If you want to jump in early, you can do so through our special VR testing branch on Steam. Thanks to everyone who has already tried the VR Beta and left us immensely valuable feedback.

[h2]How to access the VR beta in Steam[/h2]

[olist]
[*] Right click the game in Steam and open the Properties window
[*] Open Betas-tab
[*] Type "poolsvrpublicbeta" without the quotes into the text field and click the button next to it
[*] Click “opt into vr-beta-public”
[*] Steam should then download the VR beta build of the game for you
[*] You can opt in & out of the beta version from the “Beta participation” drop down menu whenever you like
[/olist]

[b]Note[/b]: VR is only available for Windows version at the moment. Unfortunately Unity game engine doesn't support building with OpenXR on Linux.

[h2]VR Beta feedback, discussion and bug reports[/h2]

Feel free to have VR mode related discussion, feedback and thoughts on [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2663530/discussions/0/4694532371788081454/]Steam Forums[/url].


If you wish to leave feedback anonymously, we’ve created a [url=https://forms.gle/95HSUywyZo3VXxFY9]Google Form[/url] where you can give your thoughts about the VR mode.


You can also always contact us at our [url=https://discord.gg/pools-1151072381478125628]Discord-server[/url] or via e-mail at support(at)tensori.fi


We're especially looking for feedback on how the VR mode works with different types of VR devices, such as Valve Index or Pico VR headsets. We’ve developed and tested the game using Meta Quest 2, 3 and a PlayStation VR2 headset on PC, so any comments about the play experience and SteamVR input rebind tool on different devices is incredibly helpful.

The VR mode has a suite of comfort and accessibility settings. We’d love to hear if you are able to find a combination of these settings that allows for a comfortable VR experience. If you’d like to see a new setting added to the VR mode, please let us know about it on this thread, feedback form, Discord-server, or e-mail.

Have fun!
[i]- Tensori[/i]

notes.title: Update notes (14th Jun 2024) - the Steam Deck update
notes.content:
Another batch of bug fixes and improvements is here! We recently got our hands on a Steam Deck and we have been testing and improving the play experience on the device.

[h3]Collaboration with UNIKAT[/h3]
Added UNIKAT label as co-publisher to Steam page. UNIKAT is a collection of independent, unique, and minimal games. It's brand new venture from Michal Napora who has helped us in marketing. No changes to relationship, we will still operate as an indie company.

[h3]General changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added graphical presets dropdown to settings menu
[*] Fixed a bug where chapter 6 autosave would not get deleted when finishing the chapter
[*] Adjusted glass material
[*] Updated localizations
[*] Changed controller trigger inputs from sprint action to camera zoom in/out actions
[*] Added camera look sensitivity multiplier to zoom action. Zooming in reduces the look sensitivity linearly depending on the level of zoom.
[*] Fixed a bug where settings menu dropdown elements would not scroll vertically when using a controller
[*] Fixed a bug where UI navigation would drop inputs when using a controller's directional pad at low frame rates
[*] Fixed positions of some spawned objects using "spawn" command from dev console
[*] Fixed a rare bug where water dripping got stuck in a loop when exiting water
[*] Loading screen now automatically skips the play button after player has finished chapter 1
[*] Adjusted camera behavior in water slides:
[list] 

[*] In bends, the camera now adapts more strongly to the shape of the slide and anticipates the player's future movement path. This improves the visual presentation of those spots where the camera would look straight ahead at a wall instead of the incoming path. [/list]
[*] Added bloom lens dirt effect toggle to the graphics settings menu
[*] Fixed incorrect controller button icons in settings menu when using certain Xbox controllers
[*] Fixed a bug where player could get stuck in air when walking on a ledge
[/list]

[h3]Steam Deck[/h3]
[list]
[*] Steam Deck has these custom graphical presets:

[list]
[*] Performance (60fps)
[*] Balanced (40fps)
[*] Quality (30fps)
[/list]
[*] Added Steam Deck input icons to settings screen
[/list]
We are also now looking into performance optimizations for "interactive water" setting to allow Steam Deck users to enable it without tanking the performance.

[h3]Linux[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed missing audio output on some Linux devices
[*] Fixed video file playback (.mp4 format was not supported)
[/list]

[h3]Notes about V-sync and target frame rate:[/h3]
In main menu screen, V-sync is disabled by default and target frame is locked to 60. This is intended behavior to prevent unnecessary system load.
In loading screens, V-sync is disabled by default and target frame is locked to 30.

If V-sync is enabled, the game's target frame rate is determined by the window mode setting and display resolution setting:

[list]
[*] [b]Fullscreen[/b]: target frame rate is current display resolution selection's maximum refresh rate
[*] [b]Borderless windowed[/b] and [b]windowed[/b]: target frame rate is [b]the maximum supported refresh rate of your display[/b] regardless of the resolution selection
[/list]
